sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Computerized Embroidery and Ultrasonic Seaming of Custom Plush Dolls

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code tradition, supplemented by Luxembourg/Belgian commercial law and EU law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BLEU–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (1984, entered into force 1986)
Luxembourg–United States Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (1996, as amended by 2009 Protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 14 July 2019 on UBO thresholds; CSSF Regulation 12-02 as amended; EU AML Directives (especially Directive (EU) 2018/843).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: General partner's certificate of incorporation and good standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the partner's foreign jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport of each natural person UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority in UBO's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residence (recent utility bill or bank statement) for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility company or regulated credit institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization with no apostille if private document; apostille if notarized

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société) or notarial deed of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary or, for private deed, law firm/registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if executed outside Luxembourg) or simply notarized in Luxembourg

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for the SCSp and/or its general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Credit institution (source of funding / relationship bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization or Hague Apostille if issued by a foreign bank

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory detection of politically exposed persons (PEPs) at national and foreign levels, with enhanced due diligence for PEP family members and close associates. Screening of all UBOs, general partners, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU terrorism and restrictive measures lists, OFAC SDN List (where relevant), and Luxembourg's national anti-money laundering / counter-terrorist financing list maintained by the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF) and the CSSF. Screening must be completed before incorporation and refreshed on any material event; records retained for five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS Luxembourg via https://www.lbr.lu (eRCS portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in Latin script; if the intended name contains non-French, non-German, or non-Luxembourgish words, it must be transliterated into Latin script and a certified translation into French, German, or Luxembourgish must be submitted for scrutiny. The name must precisely reflect the legal form, including the suffix 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale', and must not be misleading or contrary to Luxembourg public policy.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice (Ministère de la Justice) within 30 days of receipt of the refusal, and then proceed to the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within 3 months if no ministerial response. Alternatively, the applicant may request a fresh name reservation after amending the name. The procedure is governed by the Law of 15 August 1915 on commercial companies (as amended) and the Luxembourg Business Registers Act.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are acceptable for initial registration of an SCSp provided that the administrative headquarters and actual decision-making are verifiably located in Luxembourg and that sufficient substance is maintained to avoid anti-abuse challenges. A purely virtual absence of any Luxembourg operational presence may trigger regulatory or tax substance inquiries.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated probability under 5%) for a standard plastic toy OEM (ISIC 3240) with no regulated financial or fiduciary activity. Unannounced on-site inspections are unlikely but may be triggered by UBO filing inconsistencies, suspicious payment flows, or a tax/competence risk reassessment.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS name search and non-usage certificate ('attestation de non-usage du nom')
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official statutory tariff (EUR 50 + EUR 5 e-filing fee)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the SCSp in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official statutory tariff (approx. EUR 25-35 depending on filing method)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation act in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Justice (via RESA official portal)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of partnership agreement (when notarial form is chosen)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark tariff (EUR 600-1,200 depending on document length and notary fee schedule)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and/or consular legalization of foreign public documents (passports, certificates of good standing, bank references)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent foreign ministry, court, or consulate of the document's origin country
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing public fee per document (estimated 5 documents at USD 20-100 each)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/UBO KYC and PEP/sanction screening software (one-time onboarding)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed screening provider (e.g., World-Check, Refinitiv, LexisNexis)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Commercial subscription fee for a single full screening package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office service (first year, including correspondence and administrative address)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg corporate service provider / fiduciary / management company
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark (approx. EUR 450-800 depending on provider and services)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, notably Articles 1-15 and 100-142; Law of 12 July 2013 introducing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership Agreement (Contrat de Société) and Declaration of Conformity (Déclaration de Conformité)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement for an SCSp. Capital is freely determined in the partnership agreement and must be subscribed as agreed; no escrow account is mandated by Luxembourg law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: We, the undersigned initial partners of [●] SCSp, hereby approve the partnership agreement and subscriptions as set forth therein. Each partner's capital commitment is accepted in accordance with the agreed capital schedule. The registered office of the partnership is fixed at [●] Luxembourg. The first manager(s) shall be [●], who shall act as gérant(s) with full powers to conduct the partnership's business and to represent the partnership vis-à-vis third parties. All formalities with the Luxembourg Business Registers and any other authorities are hereby authorized and delegated to the gérant(s). This resolution is effective immediately upon signing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and legalization of the partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (optional unless real estate contribution) or directly by all initial partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement (SCSp contract) and have each partner execute it. Where a notary is used, ensure the notarial deed is signed and recorded. The agreement must identify the general partner(s) (gérant(s)), the nature of contributions, and the registered office in Luxembourg.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement
Valid passport or national ID of each partner
Proof of residential address of each partner
Bank reference or proof of contribution proof (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or a partner raises deficiencies, amend and re-execute the agreement; correct signatures or attachments and re-submit to the notary if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation documents with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed partnership agreement, the declaration of conformity signed by the gérant(s), and the required identification forms via the LBR online portal (www.lbr.lu) or at the RCS counter. Pay the statutory filing fee. The RCS will review for compliance and issue the registration number.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement
Declaration of conformity (déclaration de conformité)
Identity documents of the gérant(s)
Proof of registered office address in Luxembourg
RCS formation form (F-01 or equivalent electronic form)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query, respond by submitting corrected or supplementary documentation within the prescribed deadline; re-file via the same portal upon clawback or deficiency notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Electronic Compendium of Companies and Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal Publications Office (Ministry of Justice) / RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following RCS registration, the registrar will automatically refer the legal details to the RESA for publication. Verify that the required particulars (entity name, legal form, registered office, gérant(s), partnership capital) are accurately published in the official electronic compendium.
required_dossiers: No separate application required; await automatic publication reference
Registration file number from RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or contains errors, file a request with the RCS to rectify the RESA entry; provide supporting documents to substantiate the correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of gérant(s) appointment and registered office details
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon formation, formally record the appointment of the gérant(s) and the exact registered office address in the RCS file. Submit specimen signatures of authorized signatories to the RCS and, where required, to the company's bank. Establish that the registered office is physically situated in Luxembourg and registered with the local commune.
required_dossiers: Filing form for appointment of gérant(s)
Specimen signatures of each gérant and authorized signatory
Lease or ownership title of the registered office
Consent of the gérant(s) to their appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS rejects the filing, correct the completeness of the appointment form and signature pages; re-submit within the statutory cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Anti-money laundering / KYC verification and corporate bank account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and licensed credit institutions in Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the bank's client onboarding process by providing certified corporate documents, the RCS registration extract, identification of all ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs), and a description of the intended business activity. Cooperate with the bank's due diligence requests and supply any additional information required for the appropriate commercial risk tier.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate (un certificat de non-poursuite)
Certified copy of the partnership agreement
UBO declaration (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
Business plan / intended activity statement
Identity and address proofs of all partners and signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests more information, promptly provide the additional KYC documents or amend the onboarding file; consider approaching another CSSF-regulated institution if the request is unusual.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not required — the Ministry of Economy (Direction de l'industrie) does not mandate an industrial operating license for ISIC 3240 (manufacture of plush toys) under Luxembourg law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no environmental impact assessment is required for low-impact plush toy fabrication and computerised embroidery operations; the activity falls below the Category B/E thresholds of the amended EIA law of 15 May 2018.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — negligible emissions. If textile washing generates wastewater, the municipal pretreatment standards and EU Directive 2010/75/EU (Industrial Emissions Directive) do not apply at this scale; compliance with general sewer discharge regulations remains required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupational safety certification by the Labour and Mines Inspectorate (ITM) is required for embroidery machines and ultrasonic seaming equipment; fire safety clearance from the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGI) is required for premises exceeding public-access thresholds; structural inspection certificates may be requested by the local commune for industrial floor loads.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; official portals: guichet.lu, myguichet.lu, impotsdirects.public.lu, aedt.public.lu, and pbl.lu (Luxembourg Business Registers).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity, including an SCSp, obtains a Luxembourg VAT identification number by: (1) determining whether it is a taxable person under Luxembourg VAT law; (2) appointing a fiscal representative if not established in the EU and lacking an EU fixed establishment; (3) submitting the VAT registration application (Form 750) to the AEDT through MyGuichet or in person; (4) providing a foreign commercial register extract, proof of existence, evidence of the economic activity, and expected turnover figures; (5) receiving a 14-digit Luxembourg VAT identification number. For an SCSp with a Luxembourg establishment, the entity must first be registered with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) to obtain a national business number before completing VAT registration. For direct tax purposes, the fiscally transparent SCSp files partnership tax returns only if it has Luxembourg-source income or a Luxembourg permanent establishment; the partners, not the SCSp, bear income tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box election; statutory classification governs. An SCSp is by default fiscally transparent for corporate income tax purposes, with each partner taxed in its own capacity. No general hybrid-mismatch election exists under domestic law, but an advance tax ruling may be requested to confirm the SCSp's treatment for domestic and treaty purposes. The Luxembourg implementation of the EU ATAD hybrid-mismatch rules applies to cross-border structures. Municipal business tax may exceptionally arise at SCSp level where the SCSp has a Luxembourg permanent establishment and carries on a commercial activity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Luxembourg Value Added Tax (TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée), governed by the VAT Consolidation Act and EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover for Luxembourg-established small enterprises benefiting from the small-business exemption; non-established foreign entities have no threshold and must register for Luxembourg VAT before making any taxable supply in Luxembourg unless an EU OSS/IOSS regime applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not impose a real-time fiscal clearance, transaction control, or digital stamping system for B2B VAT. Electronic invoicing is permitted; business-to-government e-invoicing is required in Peppol-compliant format for certain public procurement contracts. Exporters must nonetheless retain electronic customs declarations, transport documents, and commercial records to substantiate zero-rating on audit; no automatic API clearance is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to destinations outside the European Union may be zero-rated under Luxembourg VAT law where the supplier is a taxable person, the goods are physically dispatched or transported out of the EU by the supplier or a third party acting on its behalf, and the exporter retains full documentary evidence of export within the statutory deadlines. Intangible services are zero-rated only where the place-of-supply rules place the transaction outside the Luxembourg VAT scope or where explicit zero-rating conditions for offshore services are met. Intra-Community supplies to another EU Member State are zero-rated provided the customer's valid EU VAT identification number is stated and the movement is documented.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (SAD/D.A./ENS electronic declaration accepted by Luxembourg Customs)
Bill of Lading, CMR consignment note, or airway bill evidencing physical departure from the EU
Commercial invoice and sales contract or purchase order
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment evidence showing receipt of export proceeds
Proof of arrival/receipt in the destination country, such as a signed delivery note, customs clearance certificate from the importing country, or logistics tracking evidence
Any additional contemporaneous documents requested by the AEDT during an export zero-rating audit
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT rigorously audits export zero-rating claims and may deny the 0% rate where the documentary file is incomplete, contradictory, or fraudulent. Recovered output VAT is generally clawed back together with default interest at 0.8% per month. Late filing penalties of up to 10% of the net VAT due may be imposed, while intentional or repeated fraud can attract tax penalties of up to 100% of the evaded VAT and criminal sanctions. In practice, the tax authorities require export evidence to be retained for at least ten years and may apply retrospective assessments within the statutory limitation periods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), a member of the Eurosystem wholly integrated with the European Central Bank; AML/CFT supervision and financial-sector authorisation executed by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); UN/EU targeted financial sanctions enforced through a national consolidated list published by the Ministry of Finance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies full liberalisation of capital movements under Article 63 TFEU and Directive 88/361/EEC; both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible and transferable without any FX approval, pre-registration, or conversion quota. The euro is the domestic currency, and the BCL maintains no foreign-exchange control regime. Profit remittance from the SCSp is legally unfettered: as a tax-transparent special limited partnership under the Law of 10 August 1915 (as amended), the SCSp is not subject to corporate income tax, and distributions to non-resident partners are characterised as partnership profit allocations rather than Luxembourg dividends, so no dividend-withholding gate, branch-repatriation tax, or exit tax arises. The only practical hurdles are (i) standard AML/KYC documentation, (ii) BCL balance-of-payments statistical filings for non-resident payments of EUR 12,500 or more, (iii) EU/UN sanctions-screening compliance, and (iv) contractual banking approval of the SCSp's GP signatory structure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratio in Luxembourg. A resident enterprise or SCSp may receive, retain, and resettle export proceeds indefinitely in any convertible currency (USD, CNY, EUR, etc.) without BCL approval. The sole binding requirements are: (i) balance-of-payments reporting to the BCL for each cross-border receipt or payment of EUR 12,500 or more, usually submitted by the paying or receiving bank; (ii) five-year documentary retention of the underlying trade file (commercial invoices, HS/CN 9503.00.39 customs declarations, bills of lading, Incoterms 2020 documents); and (iii) compliance with EU economic sanctions and export-control lists where the counterparty or final destination is restricted.

BGL BNP Paribas S.A. - the largest retail and corporate bank in Luxembourg
Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM for auxiliary payment corridors (supplier micro-payments, platform-pay receipts) and LOW as the sole treasury account. Under Luxembourg PSD2 transposition (Law of 21 December 2019), only a CSSF-licensed electronic money institution, a licensed payment institution, or an EEA-licensed institution validly passporting into Luxembourg may lawfully open e-money accounts. Offshore third-country EMIs without a European passport are prohibited from holding client funds for a Luxembourg entity; CSSF Circular 20/744 further requires mandatory client-asset segregation and disclosure of sub-agent arrangements. The structural blocker is the SCSp's lack of independent legal personality: e-money platforms typically require the account holder to be a legal entity and will demand a GP mandate, deed of partnership, and UBO register excerpt. Mainstream cross-border EMIs (Airwallex, MultiPass, Wise) may decline fund-like or non-corporate vehicles and cannot provide overdraft or liquidity facilities, so the primary capital escrow and trade settlement must reside with a tier-1 bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For an unregulated SCSp, Luxembourg banks uniformly require a physical KYC interview at the Luxembourg branch for the general partner (GP) or its managing director and for each authorised signatory before account activation. In-person attendance can be waived only if the GP is itself a CSSF-regulated professional (e.g., a licensed AIFM or management company), in which case a reduced regulatory dossier replaces the interview. Limited partners and ultimate beneficial owners may be identified remotely through a notarised and apostilled identity file plus a supervised live video call, provided the notarial deed of the SCSp and the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) beneficial-ownership filing are produced. Remote-only onboarding with a foreign corporate GP is, in practice, unavailable from the four principal banks (BIL, BGL BNP Paribas, BCEE, Société Générale), and Chinese banks will add a trade-compliance interview for accounts funding PRC manufacturers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Account opening by an SCSp without separate legal personality; mandate signed by an unregulated non-resident GP.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised copy of the limited partnership agreement per Article 13 of the Law of 10 August 1915 (as amended); Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register excerpt confirming the legal-personality status; RBE beneficial-ownership filing receipt from the Luxembourg Business Registers; GP board resolution and signatory mandate; Luxembourg counsel legal opinion confirming the GP's power of representation and the liability structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner is resident in a high-risk third country or is held through an opaque trust or offshore SPV; source-of-wealth cannot be demonstrated.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organisational charts to the final natural persons with percentage interests; notarised and apostilled UBO declarations, passports, and proof of residential address; three-year source-of-wealth file (bank statements, asset sale contracts, tax returns, inheritance documents); CRS and FATCA classification forms; for a trust: certified trust deed, protector and trustee identification, trustee KYC package, and a legal opinion on trust validity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital subscription perceived as round-tripping, artificial financing, or tax-motivated without commercial substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital commitment and side letter; contemporaneous business plan with 12-month cash-flow forecast; purchase orders and pro-forma invoices from the plush-toy OEM manufacturer; the investor's incorporation documents, board resolution, SWIFT MT103 origin evidence, and PRC SAFE/FDI registration where applicable; Luxembourg-compliant transfer-pricing documentation for related-party trade.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO confirmation (annual confirmation of beneficial ownership information in the RBE register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than 31 March of the calendar year following the reporting year; a nil confirmation is required even when no beneficial ownership changes occurred
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted confirmation attracts administrative fines ranging from EUR 25 to EUR 125,000; deliberate false declarations may trigger criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of responsible officers

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels au RCSL) – required only where the SCSp loses the statutory confidentiality exemption for partnerships
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL) via the LBR e-filing platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by the partners and in any event no later than seven months after the close of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registrar can impose coercive fines up to EUR 5,000 for each unfiled account; continued default grounds a court order compelling filing; partner/manager liability for resulting tax or regulatory prejudice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual municipal business tax return (déclaration de l'impôt commercial communal, IBI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), competent local tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May following the end of the taxable year when the SCSp has a calendar-year accounting period; extensions are commonly granted upon application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties and accrued interest; default assessment by the ACD; administrative fines of 10% of unpaid tax for belated returns; criminal liability in cases of intentional concealment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return (declaration annuelle de TVA) – only if the SCSp is registered for Luxembourg VAT
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 15 May following the end of the calendar year for taxpayers filing on an annual basis; additional recapitulative statements apply for intra-EU supplies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest at the legal rate plus penalties up to 10% of the overdue VAT; failure to file may lead to official VAT assessment and criminal sanctions in severe cases

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is mandatory for a Luxembourg SCSp if, for two consecutive years, it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds: balance sheet total exceeding EUR 6.25 million, net turnover exceeding EUR 12.5 million, and average workforce exceeding 50 employees. An audit obligation may also arise under the partnership agreement or if the SCSp qualifies as a public-interest entity because all general partners are limited-liability companies and the entity exceeds the SME criteria.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the annual accounts of certain legal forms (transposing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU); optional application of IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted where statutory conditions are met.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner of the SCSp must annually confirm through the LBR/RBE electronic portal that the recorded beneficial ownership data is complete and accurate. Any change in partnership interests or shareholding structure must be reported to the RBE within 15 days of the change becoming known; after each transfer, the confirmation cycle resets and must be repeated by the following 31 March. The register is public as to accurate data, but confidentiality orders are available for minors and sheltered persons.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of partners (interests and capital contributions), held by the general partner
Minutes of partners' meetings and written resolutions
Accounting books, invoices, and underlying records (seven-year retention)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 12,000 per audit (nil if exemption applies)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at the SCSp entity level because the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) is fiscally transparent (pass-through) under Luxembourg tax law; Luxembourg-source income and deductions flow through to the partners. A Luxembourg-resident corporate partner is taxed at the combined headline rate of 24.94% (17% corporate income tax + 1.19% solidarity surcharge equal to 7% of CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax for Luxembourg City). A non-resident corporate partner is taxed only on Luxembourg-source income attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment (PE) or Luxembourg real estate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The SCSp itself is not subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax. Corporate partners benefit from the Luxembourg participation exemption under Article 166 LIR: 100% exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains where the partner holds at least 10% of share capital (or acquired the participation for at least EUR 6,000,000) for an uninterrupted 12-month period; a 0.5% or 1.2% 'taxed inclusion' adjustment may apply to financial expense disallowance. The IP box under Article 50bis LIR (80% net income exemption) is grandfathered only for qualifying patents/copyright software acquired before 1 July 2021, expiring by 30 June 2026; marketing intangibles such as a plush mascot trademark are excluded from the new IP box. Tax transparency also permits partners to claim their respective DTA benefits directly.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited: tax losses may be carried forward indefinitely under Article 114 LIR. There is no carryback. Loss offset is subject to the ATAD anti-abuse rule: losses lose their offset potential where a change of control exceeding 25% occurs within 12 months and the formerly loss-making activity is discontinued. For transparent SCSp losses, the loss allocation follows the partnership agreement and is deductible only by the partner in proportion to its profit share.
